## **Pharmaceutical Manufacturers in India**

**Actiza Pharmaceutical Pvt. Ltd.** is emerging as a leader in pharmaceutical manufacturing,
exporting, and supplying from India.

“Innovate and automate, with human touch in manufacturing process to provide affordable
pharmaceutical products to make a healthier world.”  

Actiza Pharmaceutical Pvt. Ltd. follows high global standards in formulation manufacturing with
latest machinery. We are specialized in the manufacturing and exporting of [finished
formulations][64] that cater to the most demanding global needs. We are on the verge of becoming one
of the largest pharmaceutical companies in India when it comes to [contract manufacturing][65] of
[Tablets][66], [Capsules][67], [Injections][68],[Creams/Ointments][69], [Drops][70], [Infusion][71],
[Inhaler][72], [Lotion][73], [Gel][74], [Suspension / syrup][75], [Nasal Drops/Sprays][76], etc.  

The manufacturing and R&D facility of Actiza Pharmaceutical Pvt. Ltd. is located in Surat, Gujarat,
India. It contains multiple formulation facilities in close proximity that are further sub-divided
to specific zones dedicated to particular tasks. With well-established supply chain and vendor
development systems, we have built an in-house pharmaceutical ecosystem.

Our world-class manufacturing plant is equipped with modern high-speed machines and integrated
packaging lines. Our heavily automated systems include non-fill devices, collators, multi-station
tablet presses, brevetti visual inspection machines, FFS machines and high-speed vial/ampoule
filler/sealer. Our Highly professional research team works hand-in-hand with the machines to

## What is ISO Certification?

ISO certification, an acronym for International Organization for Standardization, is a globally
recognized achievement that signifies an organization’s commitment to meeting specific standards for
quality, efficiency, and customer satisfaction. This certification is not industry-specific and can
be obtained by businesses of all sizes, spanning various sectors.
ISO certification involves a meticulous process where an organization’s management systems,
processes, and procedures are thoroughly evaluated against the relevant ISO standards. These
standards ensure that a company adheres to best practices, promotes continual improvement, and
complies with legal and regulatory requirements.
Obtaining ISO certification offers many benefits. It enhances an organization’s credibility and
trustworthiness, instilling confidence in clients and stakeholders. The certification can open doors
to new business opportunities, as many clients prefer or require their partners to hold ISO
certification. Moreover, ISO-certified businesses often experience improved operational efficiency
and reduced waste.

ISO certification demonstrates a commitment to international standards, boosting credibility and
trust among stakeholders.

### Improved Efficiency:

Implementing ISO standards enhances operational efficiency, streamlines processes, and reduces
errors.

### Global Market Access

ISO certification opens doors to global markets by ensuring products and services meet international
quality standards.

### Customer Satisfaction

Meeting ISO requirements often leads to improved customer satisfaction, as products and services
consistently meet or exceed expectations.

### Regulatory Compliance

ISO certification helps organizations stay compliant with industry regulations, reducing the risk of

### Competitive Edge

Certified organizations gain a competitive advantage, showcasing their commitment to quality and
continual improvement.

### Risk Management

ISO standards emphasize risk management, helping organizations identify, assess, and mitigate risks
effectively.

### Employee Morale

ISO certification fosters a culture of quality and responsibility, boosting employee morale and
engagement.

processes, and procedures are thoroughly evaluated against the relevant ISO standards. These
standards ensure that a company adheres to best practices, promotes continual improvement, and
complies with legal and regulatory requirements.
Obtaining ISO certification offers many benefits. It enhances an organization’s credibility and
trustworthiness, instilling confidence in clients and stakeholders. The certification can open doors
to new business opportunities, as many clients prefer or require their partners to hold ISO
certification. Moreover, ISO-certified businesses often experience improved operational efficiency
and reduced waste.

### Enhanced Credibility

ISO certification demonstrates a commitment to international standards, boosting credibility and
trust among stakeholders.

### Improved Efficiency:

Implementing ISO standards enhances operational efficiency, streamlines processes, and reduces
errors.

### Global Market Access

ISO certification opens doors to global markets by ensuring products and services meet international
quality standards.

### Customer Satisfaction

Meeting ISO requirements often leads to improved customer satisfaction, as products and services
consistently meet or exceed expectations.

## Advantages of ISO certification to your business

### Regulatory Compliance

ISO certification helps organizations stay compliant with industry regulations, reducing the risk of
legal issues.

### Competitive Edge

Certified organizations gain a competitive advantage, showcasing their commitment to quality and
continual improvement.

### Risk Management

ISO standards emphasize risk management, helping organizations identify, assess, and mitigate risks
effectively.

### Employee Morale

ISO certification fosters a culture of quality and responsibility, boosting employee morale and
engagement.

## DefeatDD is sunsetting in December 2025.

Since 2010, we’ve been working to raise awareness of the burden of diarrheal disease and increase
investment in solutions. As we prepare to sunset PATH’s DefeatDD Initiative at the end of December
2025, we celebrate the remarkable progress made over the past 15 years with our fellow advocates,
partners, governments, and collaborators.

Since 2000, child deaths from diarrhea have fallen by more than 70 percent, a number that makes us
*flush *with pride—and confident in the momentum ahead.

While this site will no longer be updated after December 31, 2025, we hope you will continue to
raise your voice. We invite you to stay engaged with the amazing organizations we’ve had an
opportunity to collaborate with over the years, including but not limited to:
* 1000 Days
* Aga Khan Foundation

partners, governments, and collaborators.

Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) cares for people affected by conflict,
disease outbreaks, natural and human-made disasters, and exclusion from health care in more than 70
countries.

## Medical care where it’s needed most.

MSF teams treat a wide range of medical issues, from disease outbreaks to malnutrition to war
wounds. And we put our decades of experience to work to produce groundbreaking medical research.

When emergencies occur, MSF teams are often among the first to arrive—and the last to leave. Get an
in-depth look at our work, including the how and why of where we respond and the challenges we face.

Common questions

## Frequently asked.

What is the cheapest country to move to as an expat in 2026?+
Vietnam, Colombia, and Georgia are among the cheapest — $700–900/month including rent. Thailand
(outside Bangkok), Mexico, and Portugal's interior cities are close seconds for Western-level
comfort at a fraction of US or UK costs.
Which countries offer digital nomad visas in 2026?+
50+ countries now have dedicated nomad visas, including Portugal (D8), Spain (DNV), Thailand (DTV —
5 years), Greece, Colombia, Indonesia, Croatia, Estonia, and Brazil. Income requirements range from
$1,500/mo (Colombia) to $3,500/mo (Spain).
How much money do I need to move abroad?+
Budget 3–6 months of living expenses upfront. For affordable countries (Mexico, Vietnam, Colombia):
$5K–$10K. For Western Europe (Portugal, Spain, Germany): $15K–$25K. Include visa fees, deposits,
health insurance, and a 3-month housing cushion.
What are the best countries for expat families?+
Portugal, Spain, Malaysia, and the Czech Republic rank highest — affordable international schools,
strong public healthcare, safe neighborhoods, and clear family reunification visa paths. Singapore
and the UAE are top picks for higher-budget families.
Do I need health insurance to move abroad?+
Yes — most countries require proof of health coverage for residency visas. Options: enroll in the
local public system (once you qualify), buy international expat insurance (SafetyWing, Cigna
Global), or use local private plans. Budget $50–$300/mo depending on country and age.
How accurate is the cost-of-living data?+
Our numbers come from expats actually living in each city — not crowd-sourced estimates like Numbeo.
Data is verified against local rent indexes, supermarket receipts, and updated quarterly. Every city
page links to the primary sources we used.

## Frequently asked.

What is the cheapest country to move to as an expat in 2026?+
Vietnam, Colombia, and Georgia are among the cheapest — $700–900/month including rent. Thailand
(outside Bangkok), Mexico, and Portugal's interior cities are close seconds for Western-level
comfort at a fraction of US or UK costs.
Which countries offer digital nomad visas in 2026?+
50+ countries now have dedicated nomad visas, including Portugal (D8), Spain (DNV), Thailand (DTV —
5 years), Greece, Colombia, Indonesia, Croatia, Estonia, and Brazil. Income requirements range from
$1,500/mo (Colombia) to $3,500/mo (Spain).
How much money do I need to move abroad?+
Budget 3–6 months of living expenses upfront. For affordable countries (Mexico, Vietnam, Colombia):
$5K–$10K. For Western Europe (Portugal, Spain, Germany): $15K–$25K. Include visa fees, deposits,
health insurance, and a 3-month housing cushion.
What are the best countries for expat families?+
Portugal, Spain, Malaysia, and the Czech Republic rank highest — affordable international schools,
strong public healthcare, safe neighborhoods, and clear family reunification visa paths. Singapore
and the UAE are top picks for higher-budget families.
Do I need health insurance to move abroad?+
Yes — most countries require proof of health coverage for residency visas. Options: enroll in the
local public system (once you qualify), buy international expat insurance (SafetyWing, Cigna
Global), or use local private plans. Budget $50–$300/mo depending on country and age.
How accurate is the cost-of-living data?+
Our numbers come from expats actually living in each city — not crowd-sourced estimates like Numbeo.
Data is verified against local rent indexes, supermarket receipts, and updated quarterly. Every city
page links to the primary sources we used.

Who We Are

## A Global Alliance Born from a Single Conversation

GAZHP connects Zambian healthcare professionals living abroad with those at home — creating a
powerful bridge of expertise, mentorship, and resources to uplift Zambia's entire health system.

**Diaspora-Led, Locally Grounded** Our members span multiple countries but keep Zambia at the center
of every initiative.
**Healthcare Professionals Driving Solutions** Doctors, nurses, and allied health professionals —
not just donors — lead our programs.
**Focus on Sustainability** We build capacity so Zambia becomes self-sufficient, not dependent on
external aid.
**Founded in 2019** after Dr. David Kazhila was asked on a radio program what physicians could
contribute to Zambia. By December 2019, GAZHP was formally registered as a nonprofit.

[Read Our Full Story][18]
Core Programs

## Where We Focus Our Efforts

Our three flagship programs target the areas of greatest need in Zambia's health landscape,
combining diaspora expertise with local partnerships.

[Mental Health]
Program 01
Addiction & Mental Health

Promoting awareness and culturally relevant mental health services through local and diaspora
partnerships. Breaking the stigma and building accessible, compassionate care across Zambia.

[Cardiovascular Care]
Program 02
Cardiovascular Care

Strengthening heart care through clinical training, specialist mentorship, telemedicine
consultations, and partnerships with global cardiology experts.

[Family Medicine & Primary Care]
Program 03
Family Medicine & Primary Care

Building the backbone of Zambia's health system through training, research, and international
collaboration. Strong primary care for every community.

[View All Programs][19]
Our Approach

## Four Pillars of Impact

Everything we do flows through four core functions that ensure sustainable, accountable, and
ethically driven healthcare transformation.

### Collaborate

Connect diaspora professionals with local practitioners and communities, building bridges of
knowledge and care that span continents.

### Build Capacity

Strengthen clinical skills through training, mentorship, and continuous medical education —
empowering Zambia's own healthcare workforce.

### Innovate

Leverage technology, telemedicine, and research for improved healthcare delivery — bringing
cutting-edge solutions to underserved communities.

### Support Care Delivery

Mobilize resources and partnerships for frontline services, ensuring that life-saving care reaches
patients in the most remote areas.

# Empowering Tanzania’s Growth

Mirumbani Holdings Limited is a Tanzanian conglomerate with investments in transportation,
logistics, real estate, manufacturing, and the agriculture value chain, Building one Sector at a
Time

[ Collaborate with Us ][24]
[ Learn More ][25]

#### This Is Our result

#### Our Subsidiaries

A dynamic and diversified conglomerate with a strong presence across Tanzania’s key sectors

###### Mirumbani Carriers Limited

Transports goods across East and Central Africa, supporting regional trade and industry.

###### Mirumbani Logistics Zambia

Enhances regional supply chains with logistics services in Zambia and East Africa.

###### Mirumbani Foods Ltd

Produces and distributes high-quality consumer food products in Tanzania and neighbor countries.

###### Mirumbani Real Estates Developer Ltd

Develops and renovates commercial and residential properties across Tanzania.

###### Mirumbani Clearing and Forwarding

Provides efficient port clearing and forwarding services for imports and exports in Tanzania.

###### Mirumbani Warehousing

Offers secure, strategically located storage solutions for various goods across Tanzania.

#### Know Our Story

Mirumbani Holdings Limited is a Tanzanian conglomerate with investments in transportation,
logistics, real estate, manufacturing, and the agriculture value chain. We are dedicated to creating
sustainable solutions that enhance service delivery standards in Tanzania and across Africa. Our
ethical governance and strategic investments position us as a leader in driving the country’s
economic growth.

[ Learn More ][26]

#### Our Work Is For Your Success

At Mirumbani Holdings Limited, we are deeply committed to making a lasting and positive impact on
the communities we serve across Tanzania.

###### Economic Empowerment

Across our subsidiaries, we provide direct employment to thousands of Tanzanians, contributing
significantly to the reduction of unemployment in the regions we operate. communities.

###### Infrastructure Development

Our investments in warehousing and transportation infrastructure enhance the efficiency of supply
chains, making goods more accessible and affordable for Tanzanians. This not only supports local
businesses but also ensures that essential products reach even the most remote areas.

###### Community Development

We invest in the development of our workforce and local communities by providing training programs
that enhance skills and improve employability. Our goal is to empower individuals to achieve their
full potential and contribute meaningfully to the economy.

[ Book an Appointment ][27]

#### Core Values

Our core values form the foundation of our business operations and guide our interactions with
stakeholders, customers, and the communities we serve.

###### Sustainability

We are dedicated to promoting sustainability in all our operations. Our focus on sustainable
practices ensures that we minimize our environmental impact and contribute positively to the
communities we serve

###### Customer-Centricity

We are committed to understanding our customer needs and delivering tailored solutions that add
value to their lives.

#### Collaborate with Us

Partner with Mirumbani Holdings Limited and join us in driving innovation, sustainability, and
excellence across Tanzania’s key sectors. Together, we can create lasting impact and build a
brighter future for all.

[ Collaborate with Us ][28]

#### Get in Touch on Us.

Quotes


**Tradition**
Being offended by facts is a long human tradition.
*Megan O'Keefe - Velocity Weapon *

**Mysterious**
The most beautiful thing we can experience is the mysterious. It is the source of all true art and
science. He to whom the emotion is a stranger, who can no longer pause to wonder and stand wrapped
in awe, is as good as dead —his eyes are closed.
*Albert Einstein *

**Inspirational Quote of the Week**
Be the change that you wish to see in the world.
* Mahatma Gandhi*

**No fear**
"Don't let the fear of striking out keep you from playing the game."
*Babe Ruth*

**Basic Rule**
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, but only transformed from one form to another.
*The law of conservation of energy*

 


**Are you confused by all the conflicting messages that rush at us daily? You are not alone. **

But be aware that this also happens to less educated people (like me) who are even less able to
understand what interests are behind these messages.
Many people feel more and more helpless or ignore the obvious and run to the next strong man.
How can this be avoided in the future?

Education could help. Give the next generation a better chance. Teach them [critical thinking][156],
make them understand the connections.

### It is for Me You Everyone

# Health Insurance
# for all

# Health
# Insurance
# for all

The compulsory National Health Insurance scheme seeks to provide for a sound and reliable healthcare
financing for Zambian households and the entire health sector. 

## National Health Insurance management Authority (NHIMA)

[ About Us ][60]

### Vision

To be a provider of world class insurance for healthcare services for all.

### Mission

To provide social security and protection for our members by financing their equitable access to
quality healthcare services in a progressive, affordable & sustainable manner.

### Values

Integrity, Solidarity, Excellence, Client-focus, University, Reliability, Equity.

## Benefit Package

Learn more about the different services NHIS covers….

[ Learn More ][61]

## Learn how to register with NHIMA

Are you self employed or employed? learn more on how to register with NHIMA below.

[ Learn More ][62]

## Healthcare providers

Learn more about the different services NHIS covers….

[ Learn More ][63]

## Register your beneficiaries

Did you know you can register your spouse and 5 dependents below the age of 18? 

Learn more on how to register your beneficiaries….

[ Learn More ][64]

## Submit a complaint

Are you self employed or employed? learn more on how to register with NHIMA below.

[ Learn More ][65]

  Mall, Lusaka Zambia ][66]

## National Health Insurance management Authority (NHIMA)

[ About Us ][60]

### Vision

To be a provider of world class insurance for healthcare services for all.

### Mission

To provide social security and protection for our members by financing their equitable access to
quality healthcare services in a progressive, affordable & sustainable manner.

### Values

Integrity, Solidarity, Excellence, Client-focus, University, Reliability, Equity.

# Make healthcare universal

OpenSRP is software that helps frontline health workers manage patients and provide services to all.
Now with FHIR 🔥

[
Email info@opensrp.io for a demo
][14]

OpenSRP 2 is an open-source FHIR-native platform designed to support health systems delivering
services and collecting data offline in communities and facilities. The platform has been used in 14
country implementations (including 4 national systems) and has over 150 million patients registered
as of June 2023.

OpenSRP 2, a new version released in 2023, combines WHO health workflows with FHIR to transform how
healthcare is delivered and managed.

### New Global Immunization Product Suite

We recently released the an Electronic Immunization Registry (EIR) product suite, meant to
strengthen delivery of immunization services with OpenSRP 2.

[Read More][15]

### OpenSRP at a Glance

## 1. Understanding the Role of Pharma Regulatory Affairs

Pharmaceutical Regulatory Affairs is a multidisciplinary function within the pharmaceutical and
biotechnology industries. It plays a critical role in ensuring that all products—drugs, biologics,

# Mastering Global Regulatory Affairs in the Pharmaceutical Industry

## 1. Understanding the Role of Pharma Regulatory Affairs

Pharmaceutical Regulatory Affairs is a multidisciplinary function within the pharmaceutical and
biotechnology industries. It plays a critical role in ensuring that all products—drugs, biologics,
and medical devices—comply with the regulations and standards required by regulatory agencies across
various countries. The regulatory affairs department acts as the interface between pharmaceutical
companies and regulatory bodies such as the FDA (United States), EMA (European Union), CDSCO
(India), PMDA (Japan), and TGA (Australia). These agencies are responsible for reviewing and
approving drug applications, overseeing safety reporting, and enforcing post-approval compliance.

At its core, regulatory affairs involves the preparation, compilation, and submission of a wide
range of regulatory documents. These documents include dossiers (CTD/eCTD), product labels, periodic
safety reports, clinical trial applications, and responses to regulatory queries. In addition, the
regulatory team ensures that the company’s products are registered correctly in each market,
labeling is compliant, and pharmacovigilance systems are in place. Regulatory professionals must
stay up to date with evolving legislation and guidance documents, as non-compliance can result in
delayed product approvals, fines, or even market bans.

The scope of regulatory affairs is not limited to product approval. It extends to lifecycle
management, including post-marketing surveillance, renewals, and variations. Companies often rely on
regulatory intelligence to anticipate changes in global legislation and proactively adjust their
strategies. As global markets expand, pharmaceutical companies increasingly need to harmonize their
regulatory strategies across jurisdictions while addressing country-specific requirements. This need
gives rise to regulatory harmonization initiatives like ICH (International Council for
Harmonisation) and WHO’s collaborative registration procedures.

Ultimately, regulatory affairs ensure that patients have timely access to safe and effective
medications. It helps companies navigate a highly regulated environment, reduce compliance risks,
and bring innovations to market faster. As the regulatory landscape becomes more complex with the
advent of gene therapy, biosimilars, and personalized medicine, the demand for skilled regulatory
professionals continues to rise. For these reasons, pharma regulatory affairs are not just a support
function—they are a strategic pillar of the pharmaceutical business model.

## 2. Key Global Regulatory Authorities and Their Requirements

Pharmaceutical companies operating globally must adhere to regulatory frameworks set by each
country’s competent authority. These agencies oversee the entire lifecycle of pharmaceutical
products—from clinical trials to marketing authorization and post-market surveillance. The major
regulatory bodies include the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), European Medicines Agency
(EMA), Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) in India, the Pharmaceuticals and Medical
Devices Agency (PMDA) in Japan, and the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) in Australia. Each
agency has its own application formats, timelines, electronic submission systems, and regulatory
expectations, making it crucial for regulatory teams to adopt a tailored approach for each region.

The U.S. FDA regulates drugs, biologics, and medical devices through a robust system that includes
pre-IND (Investigational New Drug) meetings, submission of IND applications for clinical trials, and
final approval via NDA (New Drug Application) or BLA (Biologics License Application). The FDA
mandates submission in electronic format via the Electronic Submissions Gateway (ESG) using the eCTD
standard. Additionally, periodic safety reporting, annual updates, and compliance with labeling and
promotional guidelines are essential post-approval obligations.

The EMA functions under the centralized procedure, where a single application leads to marketing
authorization across all EU member states. It also supports decentralized and mutual recognition
procedures (DCP and MRP) for drugs not eligible for centralized review. EMA requires rigorous
compliance with ICH guidelines and regional documentation in Module 1 of the eCTD. Scientific
advice, orphan designation, and accelerated assessment pathways are additional features companies
can leverage to expedite approvals.

In India, CDSCO governs drug approvals under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019. All
applications—whether for clinical trial permission or marketing authorization—must be submitted
through the SUGAM portal. CDSCO places a strong emphasis on local clinical trial data, especially
for new chemical entities (NCEs). Regulatory submissions must include complete CTD modules, and
products are subject to labeling regulations and import license requirements for foreign
manufacturers. CDSCO also monitors pharmacovigilance through PvPI (Pharmacovigilance Programme of
India).

Other notable agencies include Health Canada, ANVISA (Brazil), SFDA (Saudi Arabia), and Swissmedic
(Switzerland). Some countries, like those in ASEAN, follow the ACTD (ASEAN Common Technical Dossier)
format. To manage this global diversity, many companies develop a core dossier strategy that adapts
to country-specific variations. Regulatory intelligence tools and agency guidance documents play a
critical role in maintaining compliance. Successful navigation of these agencies not only
accelerates product launches but also minimizes the risk of rejections or regulatory penalties.

## 3. The Drug Approval Process: From Development to Market Authorization

The journey of a pharmaceutical product from the laboratory to the patient’s hands involves a
multi-phase regulatory approval process. This process ensures that only safe, effective, and
high-quality drugs are made available to the public. While the specifics may vary across regulatory
jurisdictions, the fundamental framework remains largely consistent worldwide. It comprises
preclinical research, clinical trials (Phases I–III), regulatory submission, marketing
authorization, and post-market surveillance. Regulatory affairs professionals are involved at every
stage, ensuring that the data generated meet regional regulatory standards and that submissions are
complete and accurate.

The first phase, preclinical research, involves in-vitro and animal studies to establish the safety
profile of the investigational compound. Regulatory agencies require this data to approve an
Investigational New Drug (IND) application or its equivalent, which grants permission to begin human
trials. This is followed by clinical trials, which are conducted in three main phases. Phase I
assesses safety and dosage in healthy volunteers. Phase II evaluates efficacy and side effects in a
limited patient population. Phase III confirms effectiveness and monitors adverse reactions in a
larger, diverse group. Regulatory bodies may also require Phase IV or post-marketing studies to
assess long-term effects after a product is launched.

Once clinical data confirms the product’s safety and efficacy, a New Drug Application (NDA) or
Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) is submitted to the appropriate authority. These
submissions must follow specific formats—typically CTD or eCTD—and include extensive data sets
covering quality, non-clinical, and clinical components. Regulatory agencies review these
applications meticulously and may raise questions or request additional data before granting
approval. During this phase, the regulatory affairs team is responsible for managing communication
with the authority, organizing response strategies, and maintaining consistency across submitted
modules.

Approval does not signify the end of regulatory obligations. Post-approval, companies must manage
product labeling, pharmacovigilance reporting, and any lifecycle changes such as new indications,
formulation tweaks, or manufacturing site updates. Variations are classified differently depending
on the region—Type I/II in the EU or PAS/CBE in the U.S. Failure to manage these updates properly
can lead to compliance issues, warning letters, or license suspension. Hence, understanding the full
arc of the drug approval process is essential not only for regulatory compliance but also for a
successful product lifecycle strategy.

## 4. CTD and eCTD: Structure, Importance, and Global Adoption

The Common Technical Document (CTD) is an internationally recognized format for submitting
regulatory information to health authorities. Developed by the International Council for
Harmonisation (ICH), the CTD standardizes the way data is presented in drug applications, thereby
streamlining the review process for regulatory agencies and simplifying dossier preparation for
pharmaceutical companies. The CTD is organized into five modules, each with specific content
requirements. These include administrative and regional information (Module 1), summaries and
overviews (Module 2), quality-related documents (Module 3), nonclinical study reports (Module 4),
and clinical study reports (Module 5).

Module 1 is region-specific and includes forms, cover letters, labeling, and local administrative
documents. Module 2 serves as a bridge between detailed technical data and the reviewers,
summarizing the quality, nonclinical, and clinical information presented in Modules 3–5. Module 3,
often referred to as CMC (Chemistry, Manufac

# Mastering Global Regulatory Affairs in the Pharmaceutical Industry

## 1. Understanding the Role of Pharma Regulatory Affairs

Pharmaceutical Regulatory Affairs is a multidisciplinary function within the pharmaceutical and
biotechnology industries. It plays a critical role in ensuring that all products—drugs, biologics,
and medical devices—comply with the regulations and standards required by regulatory agencies across
various countries. The regulatory affairs department acts as the interface between pharmaceutical
companies and regulatory bodies such as the FDA (United States), EMA (European Union), CDSCO
(India), PMDA (Japan), and TGA (Australia). These agencies are responsible for reviewing and
approving drug applications, overseeing safety reporting, and enforcing post-approval compliance.

At its core, regulatory affairs involves the preparation, compilation, and submission of a wide
range of regulatory documents. These documents include dossiers (CTD/eCTD), product labels, periodic
safety reports, clinical trial applications, and responses to regulatory queries. In addition, the
regulatory team ensures that the company’s products are registered correctly in each market,
labeling is compliant, and pharmacovigilance systems are in place. Regulatory professionals must
stay up to date with evolving legislation and guidance documents, as non-compliance can result in
delayed product approvals, fines, or even market bans.

The scope of regulatory affairs is not limited to product approval. It extends to lifecycle
management, including post-marketing surveillance, renewals, and variations. Companies often rely on
regulatory intelligence to anticipate changes in global legislation and proactively adjust their
strategies. As global markets expand, pharmaceutical companies increasingly need to harmonize their
regulatory strategies across jurisdictions while addressing country-specific requirements. This need
gives rise to regulatory harmonization initiatives like ICH (International Council for
Harmonisation) and WHO’s collaborative registration procedures.

Ultimately, regulatory affairs ensure that patients have timely access to safe and effective
medications. It helps companies navigate a highly regulated environment, reduce compliance risks,
and bring innovations to market faster. As the regulatory landscape becomes more complex with the
advent of gene therapy, biosimilars, and personalized medicine, the demand for skilled regulatory
professionals continues to rise. For these reasons, pharma regulatory affairs are not just a support
function—they are a strategic pillar of the pharmaceutical business model.

## 2. Key Global Regulatory Authorities and Their Requirements

Pharmaceutical companies operating globally must adhere to regulatory frameworks set by each
country’s competent authority. These agencies oversee the entire lifecycle of pharmaceutical
products—from clinical trials to marketing authorization and post-market surveillance. The major
regulatory bodies include the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), European Medicines Agency
(EMA), Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) in India, the Pharmaceuticals and Medical
Devices Agency (PMDA) in Japan, and the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) in Australia. Each
agency has its own application formats, timelines, electronic submission systems, and regulatory
expectations, making it crucial for regulatory teams to adopt a tailored approach for each region.

The U.S. FDA regulates drugs, biologics, and medical devices through a robust system that includes
pre-IND (Investigational New Drug) meetings, submission of IND applications for clinical trials, and
final approval via NDA (New Drug Application) or BLA (Biologics License Application). The FDA
mandates submission in electronic format via the Electronic Submissions Gateway (ESG) using the eCTD
standard. Additionally, periodic safety reporting, annual updates, and compliance with labeling and
promotional guidelines are essential post-approval obligations.

The EMA functions under the centralized procedure, where a single application leads to marketing
authorization across all EU member states. It also supports decentralized and mutual recognition
procedures (DCP and MRP) for drugs not eligible for centralized review. EMA requires rigorous
compliance with ICH guidelines and regional documentation in Module 1 of the eCTD. Scientific
advice, orphan designation, and accelerated assessment pathways are additional features companies
can leverage to expedite approvals.

In India, CDSCO governs drug approvals under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019. All
applications—whether for clinical trial permission or marketing authorization—must be submitted
through the SUGAM portal. CDSCO places a strong emphasis on local clinical trial data, especially
for new chemical entities (NCEs). Regulatory submissions must include complete CTD modules, and
products are subject to labeling regulations and import license requirements for foreign
manufacturers. CDSCO also monitors pharmacovigilance through PvPI (Pharmacovigilance Programme of
India).

Other notable agencies include Health Canada, ANVISA (Brazil), SFDA (Saudi Arabia), and Swissmedic
(Switzerland). Some countries, like those in ASEAN, follow the ACTD (ASEAN Common Technical Dossier)
format. To manage this global diversity, many companies develop a core dossier strategy that adapts
to country-specific variations. Regulatory intelligence tools and agency guidance documents play a
critical role in maintaining compliance. Successful navigation of these agencies not only
accelerates product launches but also minimizes the risk of rejections or regulatory penalties.

## 3. The Drug Approval Process: From Development to Market Authorization

The journey of a pharmaceutical product from the laboratory to the patient’s hands involves a
multi-phase regulatory approval process. This process ensures that only safe, effective, and
high-quality drugs are made available to the public. While the specifics may vary across regulatory
jurisdictions, the fundamental framework remains largely consistent worldwide. It comprises
preclinical research, clinical trials (Phases I–III), regulatory submission, marketing
authorization, and post-market surveillance. Regulatory affairs professionals are involved at every
stage, ensuring that the data generated meet regional regulatory standards and that submissions are
complete and accurate.

The first phase, preclinical research, involves in-vitro and animal studies to establish the safety
profile of the investigational compound. Regulatory agencies require this data to approve an
Investigational New Drug (IND) application or its equivalent, which grants permission to begin human
trials. This is followed by clinical trials, which are conducted in three main phases. Phase I
assesses safety and dosage in healthy volunteers. Phase II evaluates efficacy and side effects in a
limited patient population. Phase III confirms effectiveness and monitors adverse reactions in a
larger, diverse group. Regulatory bodies may also require Phase IV or post-marketing studies to
assess long-term effects after a product is launched.

Once clinical data confirms the product’s safety and efficacy, a New Drug Application (NDA) or
Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) is submitted to the appropriate authority. These
submissions must follow specific formats—typically CTD or eCTD—and include extensive data sets
covering quality, non-clinical, and clinical components. Regulatory agencies review these
applications meticulously and may raise questions or request additional data before granting
approval. During this phase, the regulatory affairs team is responsible for managing communication
with the authority, organizing response strategies, and maintaining consistency across submitted
modules.

Approval does not signify the end of regulatory obligations. Post-approval, companies must manage
product labeling, pharmacovigilance reporting, and any lifecycle changes such as new indications,
formulation tweaks, or manufacturing site updates. Variations are classified differently depending
on the region—Type I/II in the EU or PAS/CBE in the U.S. Failure to manage these updates properly
can lead to compliance issues, warning letters, or license suspension. Hence, understanding the full
arc of the drug approval process is essential not only for regulatory compliance but also for a
successful product lifecycle strategy.

## 4. CTD and eCTD: Structure, Importance, and Global Adoption

The Common Technical Document (CTD) is an internationally recognized format for submitting
regulatory information to health authorities. Developed by the International Council for
Harmonisation (ICH), the CTD standardizes the way data is presented in drug applications, thereby
streamlining the review process for regulatory agencies and simplifying dossier preparation for
pharmaceutical companies. The CTD is organized into five modules, each with specific content
requirements. These include administrative and regional information (Module 1), summaries and
overviews (Module 2), quality-related documents (Module 3), nonclinical study reports (Module 4),
and clinical study reports (Module 5).

Module 1 is region-specific and includes forms, cover letters, labeling, and local administrative

is keen on enhancing trade with other countries and easing procedures for exporting and importing of

The IMF last week forecast Zambia’s economy will contract by 3.5% in 2020, from the growth of 1.5%
in 2019, as the coronavirus pandemic hits economies across the world. Zambia’s economic activity has
also been hampered by widespread power shortages.“Zambia will now discuss with the fund on an
appropriate macro-economic framework that will lead to a program eventually,” Ng’andu told

had already embarked on measures including reduced borrowing and the suspension of some projects.

## UNICEF’s work

UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children's lives, to defend their rights,
and to help them fulfil their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. And we never give
up.

# Adventure awaits - before they go, consider cholera protection

## Why VAXCHORA?¹

### Indication and usage

VAXCHORA is a vaccine indicated for active immunization against disease caused by Vibrio cholerae
serogroup O1 in persons 2 through 64 years of age traveling to cholera-affected areas.

**Limitations of Use:** The effectiveness of VAXCHORA has not been established in persons living in
cholera-affected areas. The effectiveness of VAXCHORA has not been established in persons who have
pre-existing immunity due to previous exposure to V. cholerae or receipt of a cholera vaccine.
VAXCHORA has not been shown to protect against disease caused by V. cholerae serogroup O139 or other
non-O1 serogroups.

**The Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) recommends VAXCHORA for people 2 through
64 years of age who are traveling to an area with active cholera transmission.^{2*}**

To read the full recommendation and see the most recent updates, visit the CDC website.

[Read CDC Recommendation Here][14]

*The CDC considers cholera transmission to be active in a country when any of the following criteria
are met:
* • WHO reports a cholera outbreak (e.g., annual reports, outbreak bulletins, disease outbreak news)
  • A country reports more than 100 suspected cholera cases in the previous 12 months as documented
  by reliable, publicly available sources such as WHO or the Ministries of Health
  • CDC experts have reviewed available information and have determined that cholera is likely
  present even if not officially reported

CDC, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; WHO, World Health Organization.

moderate to severe diarrhea following challenge at 10 days and 3 months post-vaccination.^{1,3,a,b}

randomized 3:1 to receive 1 dose of VAXCHORA or placebo.¹

years of age in Study 1.

[cohort-1]

In the 10-day challenge group, 2 volunteers receiving VAXCHORA (2/35, 5.7%) developed moderate to
severe diarrhea after challenge with *V. cholerae*.¹

#### Cohort 2

66 healthy volunteers received VAXCHORA (N=33) or placebo (N=33) in the 3-month challenge¹

Efficacy **3 months** after vaccination¹

[cohort-2]

In the 3-month challenge group, 4 volunteers taking VAXCHORA (4/33, 12.1%) developed moderate to
severe diarrhea after challenge with*V. cholerae*.¹

#### In the case of each cohort (10-day and 3-month), evaluation of the relative efficacy of
#### VAXCHORA was made in comparison to the combined outcomes among recipients of placebo in both
#### cohorts.¹

#### The majority of placebo recipients (39/66, 59.1%) developed moderate or severe diarrhea after
#### being challenged with V. cholerae.¹
* ^{a} Moderate to severe diarrhea defined as ≥3.0 L or ≥5.0 L, respectively, within 10 days after
  being challenged with *V. cholerae* 01 El Tor Inaba.³
* ^{b} Vaccine efficacy=[(Attack Rate in Placebo Group – Attack Rate in Vaccine Group)/Attack Rate
  in Placebo Group] x 100.

#### Immunogenicity (seroconversion) Trials — Studies 1, 4, and 5

A series of immunogenicity trials further contributed to the demonstration of VAXCHORA's efficacy,
particularly in other age groups than were enrolled in Study 2. In these studies, immune response to
VAXCHORA was based on seroconversion. A vibriocidal antibody assay was used to measure serum levels
of neutralizing antibodies against the vaccine strain (classical Inaba), and seroconversion was
defined as a ≥4-fold rise in serum vibriocidal antibody from baseline to 10 days post vaccination.
Based on an observed association in Study 2 (the challenge study in adults aged 18-45 years) between
seroconversion and protection from V. cholerae disease, seroconversion rate at 10 days
post-vaccination was used to evaluate response to vaccination in these immunogenicity trials.¹

#### Study 1 — Immunogenicity Study in Adults Aged 18-45

**Study Design:** Study 1 was a randomized, double-blind, saline placebo-controlled safety and
immunogenicity study conducted in the US and Australia. A total of 3146 subjects 18 through 45 years
of age not previously exposed to cholera were randomized 8:1 to receive 1 dose of VAXCHORA or
placebo.¹

Seroconversion occurred in 93.5% of vaccine recipients versus 4% of placebo recipients 10 days after
vaccination¹

Seroconversion after **10 days**

[cohort-3]

#### Seroconversion rates (95% CI) were: vaccine recipients, 93.5% (92.5%, 94.4%); placebo, 4% (2%,
#### 7%).¹

#### Study 4 — Immunogenicity Study in Adults Aged 46-64

**Study Design:** Study 4 was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled safety and
immunogenicity study conducted in the US. A total of 398 subjects 46 through 64 years of age with no
prior history of cholera infection or travel to a cholera-endemic area in the previous 5 years were
randomized 3:1 to receive 1 dose of VAXCHORA or placebo.¹

Vibriocidal antibody seroconversion rates for the classical Inaba strain were compared at 10 days
post-vaccination between subjects 46 through 64 years of age in Study 4 and subjects 18 through 45
years of age in Study 1.

VAXCHORA demonstrated a seroconversion rate of 90.4% in adults 46 through
64 years of age¹

**Study Design:** Study 5 was a randomized, double-blind, saline placebo-controlled safety and

<12 years of age; Cohort 3: 2 to <6 years of age.¹

Classical Inaba vibriocidal antibody seroconversion rates at 10 days post-vaccination were compared

## FAQs

Is Visagov legitimate?

Yes, absolutely. Visagov is a 100% legitimate visa management platform with a proven track record in
our sector, with many years of experience and over 700,000 visas successfully processed.

We are a Spanish company based in Barcelona, operating under the legal entity ByteTravel SA (NIF:
A42788984). We ensure the highest standards of data protection in accordance with current GDPR
regulations, providing our clients with the best service with transparency, efficiency and
reliability. This is also the reason why many travel agencies and major tourism groups have trusted
us to become their official partner for all their visa processing needs.

Our team of experts is always available to provide assistance and ensure a smooth process from start
to finish. At Visagov, we’re with you every step of the way.

What payment methods are available?
You can pay with your credit, debit or prepaid card. There are plenty of other options to choose
from, including PayPal, Revolut Pay, Amazon Pay, Google Pay, Alipay and MobilePay.
Is my eVisa refundable?

The answer will depend on the status of your application. If your eVisa has already been approved,
you will not be eligible for a refund.

For more information, head to our [Refund policy][84].

Are my personal details safe?

Yes, we comply rigorously with GDPR regulations.

Any personal information you provide will only be used to process your application. It will never be
shared with any third parties or used for other purposes.

For more information, head to our [Privacy policy][85].

How long will it take to receive a decision on my application? Can I track its progress?

It depends on the document you selected. In most cases, a decision is made within the first 24-48
hours. We also offer urgent processing for specific destinations, which ensures you receive your
approved eVisa in less than 24 hours.

After your application is approved, we will send the official document to the email address of your
choice.

You can always track the progress of your application in our [Status checker][86].

If you would like an invoice for your order, contact us detailing your application ID and we will
send it directly to you.

Can I change the details of my application?

It will not be possible if your application has already been approved.

If you need to change any information, please contact us with the specific details of your case, and
we will check whether modifications are still possible.

I want to cancel my application, how can I proceed?

It will always depend on the status of your application. If it has already been approved, it will
not be possible to proceed with the cancellation.

If you wish to cancel it, contact us with your application ID and we will check your case.

What do I do if my visa is rejected?
If your visa is denied by the authorities, Visagov will give you a full refund of all government
fees. However, our processing fee will never be refunded.
If I am denied a visa once, can I reapply?

In case of a rejected application, you will need to go to the corresponding embassy in person to
find out the reasons why and whether you are allowed to enter the country.

To reapply, the only option available is to do so at the embassy.

How will I receive my visa?
If it is approved, we will send you the official document in PDF format to the email address you
provided in your application form.
What type of passport is valid for an eVisa?

You are only allowed to apply with an ordinary passport.

If your passport is not ordinary, you will need to check if your destination accepts it, as well as
the specific requirements and eligibility criteria for your type of passport.

## FAQs

Is Visagov legitimate?

Yes, absolutely. Visagov is a 100% legitimate visa management platform with a proven track record in
our sector, with many years of experience and over 700,000 visas successfully processed.

We are a Spanish company based in Barcelona, operating under the legal entity ByteTravel SA (NIF:
A42788984). We ensure the highest standards of data protection in accordance with current GDPR
regulations, providing our clients with the best service with transparency, efficiency and
reliability. This is also the reason why many travel agencies and major tourism groups have trusted
us to become their official partner for all their visa processing needs.

Our team of experts is always available to provide assistance and ensure a smooth process from start
to finish. At Visagov, we’re with you every step of the way.

What payment methods are available?
You can pay with your credit, debit or prepaid card. There are plenty of other options to choose
from, including PayPal, Revolut Pay, Amazon Pay, Google Pay, Alipay and MobilePay.
Is my eVisa refundable?

The answer will depend on the status of your application. If your eVisa has already been approved,
you will not be eligible for a refund.

For more information, head to our [Refund policy][84].

Are my personal details safe?

Yes, we comply rigorously with GDPR regulations.

Any personal information you provide will only be used to process your application. It will never be
shared with any third parties or used for other purposes.

For more information, head to our [Privacy policy][85].

How long will it take to receive a decision on my application? Can I track its progress?

It depends on the document you selected. In most cases, a decision is made within the first 24-48
hours. We also offer urgent processing for specific destinations, which ensures you receive your
approved eVisa in less than 24 hours.

After your application is approved, we will send the official document to the email address of your
choice.

You can always track the progress of your application in our [Status checker][86].

If you would like an invoice for your order, contact us detailing your application ID and we will
send it directly to you.

Can I change the details of my application?

It will not be possible if your application has already been approved.

If you need to change any information, please contact us with the specific details of your case, and
we will check whether modifications are still possible.

I want to cancel my application, how can I proceed?

It will always depend on the status of your application. If it has already been approved, it will
not be possible to proceed with the cancellation.

If you wish to cancel it, contact us with your application ID and we will check your case.

What do I do if my visa is rejected?
If your visa is denied by the authorities, Visagov will give you a full refund of all government
fees. However, our processing fee will never be refunded.
If I am denied a visa once, can I reapply?

In case of a rejected application, you will need to go to the corresponding embassy in person to
find out the reasons why and whether you are allowed to enter the country.

To reapply, the only option available is to do so at the embassy.

How will I receive my visa?
If it is approved, we will send you the official document in PDF format to the email address you
provided in your application form.
What type of passport is valid for an eVisa?

You are only allowed to apply with an ordinary passport.

If your passport is not ordinary, you will need to check if your destination accepts it, as well as
the specific requirements and eligibility criteria for your type of passport.

# Vaccinating *Africa*
# From Within

Establishing Africa's first thermostable, locally manufactured animal vaccine facility — reducing
import dependence, protecting food security, and positioning Zambia as a regional biosecurity hub
across Southern Africa.

US$12–13M
Annual Vaccine Imports · Zambia
US$1–2M
Feasibility Funding Sought
SADC
Regional Export Target
Background & Rationale

## A Critical Gap in Southern Africa's Animal Health System

Zambia's animal production sector — spanning smallholder and commercial poultry and livestock — is a
critical engine of food security, rural income, and national economic growth. Yet recurrent disease
outbreaks continue to erode productivity and sustain deep dependence on imported veterinary
vaccines.

Imported vaccines are frequently ill-matched to locally circulating strains and are constrained by
fragile cold-chain infrastructure, severely limiting their effectiveness in rural and pastoral
settings where disease pressure is highest.

This initiative proposes the establishment of a **thermostable animal vaccine R&D and manufacturing
facility** in Zambia — structured through a public-private partnership model under a hybrid
university-based incubation and joint-venture governance framework, with the Industrial Development
Corporation (IDC) of Zambia as primary institutional anchor.

Local manufacturing will reduce import dependence, improve vaccine effectiveness under field
conditions, create high-quality scientific employment, and position Zambia as a regional vaccine
supply hub across Southern Africa. The project aligns with Zambia's national industrialization goals
and strengthens global One Health, biosecurity, and pandemic prevention frameworks.

Strategic Impact Areas

## Four Pillars of Transformational Impact

One Health infrastructure that creates economic value, protects livelihoods, and builds lasting
regional capacity.

01

### Food Security

Protecting poultry and livestock from devastating disease outbreaks that erode smallholder
livelihoods and commercial operations across Zambia.

02

### Economic Growth

Skilled scientific employment and import substitution across the vaccine value chain, retaining
economic value within Zambia's borders.

03

### Pandemic Prevention

Strengthening One Health biosecurity at the animal–human interface, reducing spillover risk and
aligning with global health security frameworks.

04

### Regional Leadership

Positioning Zambia as the SADC hub for thermostable animal vaccines — exporting cold-chain-free
solutions to neighboring countries.

Priority Vaccines — Phase 1

## Two Diseases. Transformational Impact.

Phase 1 focuses on the two highest-burden, highest-impact diseases in Zambia's animal health
landscape.

Priority 1

### Newcastle Disease Vaccine

Target: Poultry (Chickens)
* 30–50% seroprevalence in Zambian backyard flocks
* Over 10 million village chickens targeted in national campaigns
* Thermostable, strain-matched NDV will be transformative
* Cold-chain-free rural deployment at the core
Priority 2

### Foot & Mouth Disease Vaccine

Target: Livestock (Cattle, Pigs)
* Affects cattle, pigs, and all cloven-hoofed livestock
* Restricts export markets and livestock trade across SADC
* Genotype-matched formulation critical for herd protection
* Thermostable platform enables deployment in remote areas

### Future Pipeline

The facility is designed with modular, scalable architecture to accommodate future expansion into
Infectious Bursal Disease (IBD), Infectious Bronchitis (IB), Avian Influenza (AI), and other
high-priority diseases as capacity and market demand grow.

Implementation Roadmap

## Four Phases to Commercial Launch

A disciplined, milestone-driven pathway from feasibility to commercial-scale thermostable vaccine
production.

1
Months 1–6

### Foundation Setting
* Convene inaugural Steering Committee; ratify Terms of Reference and MOUs with all seven members
* Prioritize donors: USTDA, USAID/DFC, Afreximbank, Gates Foundation
* Engage IDC Zambia leadership; align on joint venture rationale, equity structure, and governance
  rights
* Formalize Letter of Intent between BIOVAC Nepal and IDC Zambia; evaluate SPV options

2
Months 4–12

### Resource Mobilization
* Prepare and submit comprehensive feasibility proposals to USTDA, USAID, DFC, and priority donors
* Develop detailed US$1–2M feasibility budget with cost-benefit projections
* Register co-owned operating company in Zambia under IDC joint structure
* Recruit Zambia-based core team: veterinary scientist, regulatory officer, lab technician,
  coordinator

✦ Milestone: Feasibility funding secured — US$1–2M · 2+ agreements executed · Project formally
commenced
3
Year 1–2

### Feasibility Assessment
* Commission comprehensive NDV burden assessment: sero-prevalence, outbreak frequency, circulating
  genotypes
* Assess FMD

##### abundant wildlife and untamed wilderness – all in one friendly country.
##### 
##### Blessed with awe-inspiring natural wonders, a plethora of wildlife, huge bodies of water and
##### vast open spaces, Zambia offers unforgettable holidays exploring the real Africa.
##### 
##### Acknowledged as one of the safest countries in the world to visit, Zambia’s welcoming people
##### live in peace and harmony.
##### 
##### And here, in the warm heart of Africa, you will find some of the finest safari experiences on
##### the planet, including face-to-face encounters with nature at its most untrammelled.
##### Spectacular waterways provide adrenaline thrills or a leisurely playground for all ages. The

##### The land of the legendary African walking safari, Victoria Falls, the wild Zambezi River,
##### abundant wildlife and untamed wilderness – all in one friendly country.
##### 
##### Blessed with awe-inspiring natural wonders, a plethora of wildlife, huge bodies of water and
##### vast open spaces, Zambia offers unforgettable holidays exploring the real Africa.
##### 
##### Acknowledged as one of the safest countries in the world to visit, Zambia’s welcoming people
##### live in peace and harmony.
##### 
##### And here, in the warm heart of Africa, you will find some of the finest safari experiences on
##### the planet, including face-to-face encounters with nature at its most untrammelled.
##### Spectacular waterways provide adrenaline thrills or a leisurely playground for all ages. The

#####

### What we do

## Regulation

The Zambia Medicines Regulatory Authority is a Statutory National Medicines Regulatory Body in
Zambia established under an Act of Parliament to regulate and control the Manufacture, Importation,
Storage, Distribution, Supply, Sale and Use of Medicines and Allied Substances. 

[ [Product Registration] ][166]

Registering Safe, Quality and Effective Health Products in Zambia Product Registration is the
regulatory process through which ZAMRA evaluates and approves medicines, medical devices, cosmetics,
veterinary medicines, and allied substances before they can be imported, distributed, supplied, or
sold in Zambia. This process ensures that all regulated products meet the required standards of

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) is a system of quality assurance that ensures medicines, medical
devices, cosmetics, and other regulated health products are consistently manufactured and controlled
according to established quality standards. GMP is designed to minimize risks associated with
production that cannot be eliminated through testing of the final product alone. Compliance with GMP

Medical Devices and Allied Substances are regulated to ensure they meet the required standards of

within the country. Effective regulation protects patients, healthcare professionals, and the public
while supporting access to safe and reliable healthcare technologies. Medical devices include

regulated to ensure that only safe, effective, and quality medicines and health products enter or
leave the country. Regulatory oversight helps protect public health by preventing the circulation of
counterfeit, substandard, or unregistered products while facilitating legitimate international

The Laboratory Services Directorate provides scientific testing, analysis, and evaluation services

The Monitoring the Safety of Medicines programme is responsible for the continuous assessment and
monitoring of the safety of medicines after they have been authorized for use. Through

The Zambia Medicines Regulatory Authority is a Statutory National Medicines Regulatory Body in
Zambia established under an Act of Parliament to regulate and control the Manufacture, Importation,
Storage, Distribution, Supply, Sale and Use of Medicines and Allied Substances.
